prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules induce a ternary complex that brings an E3 ubiquitin ligase to a chosen protein and destroys it catalytically, through the PROTAC concept and the identification of cereblon as the ligase target of molecular glue degraders

statement.case_for: After reading the full first-round exchange I keep B020 as the whole prize, with Crews, Deshaies and Handa. Six of eight configurations include targeted protein degradation and no one disputes its scientific validity or independent reproduction. The principle is specific: a small molecule induces a ligase-target ternary complex and the cell destroys the target, so pharmacology becomes event-driven and catalytic instead of occupancy-based, and proteins without a binding pocket become reachable. That principle is the common ground of both strands in the citation. The PROTAC concept (Crews, Deshaies) is the designed, heterobifunctional form of it, and the cereblon identification (Handa) is the mechanistic account of the glue form, which had been used clinically for years without being understood. Ciulli's VHL ligands made the concept a design discipline, and I regard his omission as a real cost, but the citation is for the founding concept and the mechanism that defines the modality, not for every later developer. A single part keeps the three-person limit honest and lets the citation name a chemical principle, which also answers the worry that this is Medicine's prize: the achievement is molecular design of induced proximity and the structural chemistry of ligase-substrate recognition.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC is approved, so the part rests on concept, structures and independent reproduction and not on delivered medicines. Attribution remains contested: Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito all have credible claims, and Sakamoto as first author of the 2001 paper is the hardest omission. Aqvist and Chabes can fairly say that joining the heterobifunctional and glue lineages is a compromise between two histories. Base editing (B047) has stronger early clinical use, and Car-Parrinello (B061) and C-N coupling (B044) are older and have cleaner credit, so a committee that weights maturity above novelty could reasonably wait one year on B020.

responses.point: Aqvist prefers Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, arguing that Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures made rational degrader design possible, whereas cereblon explains drugs found empirically, and he would accept the glue strand only with a citation covering both modalities.
responses.response: His argument that Ciulli turned the idea into engineering is persuasive and I did not weigh it enough in round 1. I still keep Handa, for two reasons. First, the citation I propose now names the shared mechanism, ligase recruitment into a ternary complex, which is what both strands explain, so the empirical origin of thalidomide does not make cereblon a lesser discovery: Handa's work is what showed that a small molecule can redirect an E3 ligase to new substrates, and without it the glue strand is only a clinical accident. Second, four of the six B020 supporters name Handa and none other than Aqvist names Ciulli, so the third seat is where the committee can agree. His own condition, a citation explicitly covering both modalities, is met by my wording. I regard Ciulli as the strongest omitted name and will say so in the committee record. I also hold B061 as an alternative for the case in which B020 attribution cannot be settled.

responses.point: Chabes proposes two parts, base editing for Liu alone and PROTACs for Crews and Deshaies only, with no third degrader name.
responses.response: I agree that Liu alone is the defensible attribution for B047, and I accept his point that deamination without strand cleavage is a different chemical principle from nuclease cutting. I do not accept the two-part prize. Pairing two young, therapeutic-adjacent fields into one year reads as presentist, which he concedes himself, and it forces the degrader part to be a cut-down version that leaves out the mechanistic half of the modality. If the committee prefers two parts, B047 becomes more persuasive once base-editing clinical outcomes mature and the Kondo and Nishida cytidine-deamination priority question is settled, and I would then rather pair it with a different part than shrink B020. I keep B047 as my first alternative.

responses.point: Brzezinski agrees with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, argues the part of the field that is early is PROTACs and not the principle since lenalidomide-class glues are established drugs, and warns that B020 could be seen as a Medicine achievement.
responses.response: His timing point is a good one and I adopt it: the glue half of the citation is already clinically proven and the cereblon mechanism is structurally confirmed, so a missing PROTAC approval weakens only one strand and not the principle. On the Medicine overlap, I think his worry is answered by wording the citation around the chemistry, induced proximity and ternary-complex recognition, and not around therapeutic outcome. Medicine would recognise a drug, whereas here the committee recognises a way of designing molecules. I would be glad to hear whether he thinks that wording is enough.

responses.point: Somfai ranks C-N coupling first on maturity and clean two-person credit, and says he would support B047 only as a second part, not in place of a mature synthetic method.
responses.response: I take the maturity and attribution points seriously, and B044 has the cleanest credit on the list. My difficulty is still novelty: the 2010 prize recognised palladium cross-coupling as a principle, and Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work makes the C-N priority story less tidy than Buchwald and Hartwig alone suggest. He himself names B020 as an alternative and concedes it has the stronger claim for a new conceptual direction, so we may differ more on timing than on substance. I would ask whether he regards a missing PROTAC approval as a reason to prefer B044 this year, since Brzezinski has argued that the early part is PROTACs, not the principle.

responses.point: Aili moved from Ciulli to Handa as the third name but presses that omitting Ciulli is a real cost and that the citation should credit the field broadly instead of implying that the three are the only contributors.
responses.response: I agree and have changed the citation to say that the three are credited for the founding concept and for the mechanism of cereblon, with the field's wider development described as a field. I think this is the honest way to handle the three-person limit, and it is the same reasoning Sparr gives for why Ciulli and Gray are major developers after the concept was set. I do not think wording can make Sakamoto and Kim's omission comfortable, and I would not claim that it does.

uncertainties: Whether Handa or Ciulli should hold the third seat, and whether the cereblon and PROTAC strands are one achievement or two lineages joined for convenience.
Whether the absence of an approved PROTAC makes 2026 early, or whether established cereblon-based glue drugs make the principle mature enough.
Whether base editing is distinct enough from 2020 CRISPR and whether the Kondo and Nishida cytidine-deamination claim changes the Liu-only attribution.
Whether a mature, cleanly credited prize such as B061 should take precedence if B020 attribution cannot be settled.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict to disclose beyond round 1. I am a physicist at Lund University with no connection to Crews, Deshaies, Handa or any other shortlisted candidate. Somfai and Sparr are Lund colleagues; none of us regards this as a recusal issue. Sparr and Brzezinski have flagged proximity to B010, B024 and B028, none of which is in my preferred configuration.
